title: Size Charts for Personalized Products: How to Stop Costly Remakes
summary: Wrong sizes on custom orders can't be resold. Learn how to show size charts on personalized products and stop costly remakes.
body_markdown:
When that shirt has a kid's name and jersey number printed on the back, the wrong size is a loss. Nobody else wants it. You either pay for a remake or end up with an unhappy customer, and sometimes a chargeback.


That's why sizing deserves more attention on[personalized products](https://www.customily.com/) than anywhere else in your store. This guide covers where sizing goes wrong on custom orders and how to show size information so shoppers pick the right size before they spend five minutes designing.


## Why sizing mistakes cost more on personalized products


On a standard product, a sizing error is a logistics problem. On a personalized product, it's a margin problem:


- **You can't restock it.** A shirt with someone's name on it has a resale value of zero.
- **A remake doubles your cost.** You pay again for the blank, the print, and the shipping.
- **Timing matters.** Many personalized items are gifts for a specific date. A remake that arrives after the birthday doesn't fix the problem.
- **Strict return policies cut both ways.** Most stores don't accept returns on custom items. That protects you, but it also makes careful shoppers hesitate, and a hesitant shopper often leaves without buying.


The fix isn't a looser return policy. It's giving shoppers enough sizing information that they feel confident ordering.


## Where sizing goes wrong on custom orders


Most sizing problems come from a few predictable gaps:


- **The size chart is hard to find.** It sits on a separate page, in the footer, or at the bottom of a long description.
- **One chart covers every product.** Different blanks from different suppliers fit differently, but the store uses a single generic chart.
- **Shoppers pick their "usual" size.** A Medium from one brand isn't a Medium from another.
- **Units get mixed up.** International shoppers read inches as centimeters, or the other way around.
- **Size is an afterthought.** The shopper puts all their effort into the design and picks a size in two seconds at the end.
- **The buyer isn't the wearer.** Gift buyers often guess the recipient's size.


Each of these can be solved on the product page.


## 8 ways to show sizing on personalized products


**1. Put the size chart next to the size selector**


The size chart should be one click away from the place where the shopper chooses a size. A "Size chart" link or button right beside the size options works far better than a link in the footer. If shoppers have to leave the product page to find measurements, many won't bother.


**2. Use a chart for each product, not one for the whole store**


If you sell hoodies from one supplier and T-shirts from another, they need separate charts. For print-on-demand products, use the measurements for that exact blank. The Gildan 5000 and the Bella+Canvas 3001 are both sold as "unisex T-shirts," but the Bella+Canvas runs noticeably slimmer. Clean Size Charts has a library of[ready-made size charts for popular POD blanks](https://www.cleansizecharts.com/pages/blank-apparel-size-charts) , so you don't have to build each one from the supplier's spec sheet. A generic "standard sizing" chart is often worse than no chart, because it gives shoppers false confidence.


**3. Show product measurements and explain how to measure**


List the real measurements of the product (chest width, length, sleeve), not just S/M/L. Then add a short note or simple diagram on how to check them. One of the easiest methods: "Lay a shirt that fits you well flat and measure it across the chest." Shoppers can compare that number to your chart in under a minute.


**4. Offer both centimeters and inches**


If you sell internationally, show both units or let shoppers switch between them. It's a small detail that prevents a whole category of mistakes.


**5. Add fit notes in plain language**


Numbers don't tell the whole story. A short fit note answers the questions shoppers actually have:


- "Runs small. If you're between sizes, size up."
- "Unisex fit. Women may want to size down one."
- "Relaxed, oversized fit."
- "Pre-shrunk cotton, minimal shrinkage after washing."


Put the fit note near the size selector, not buried in the description.


**6. Help unsure shoppers with a size recommendation**


Some shoppers will never read a size chart, especially on mobile. For them, a[size recommender](https://www.cleansizecharts.com/pages/feature-ai-recommender) removes the guesswork.[Clean Size Charts](https://www.cleansizecharts.com/) , a Shopify size chart app, asks shoppers a few quick questions (height, weight, age and preferred fit) and matches their answers to that product's own size chart to suggest a size. Shoppers who prefer the numbers still get the full chart, with a cm/inch toggle and fit notes.


On personalized products, it also matters *how* the chart opens. A popup on the product page lets shoppers check their size without leaving the page and losing the design they've started.


Whichever tool you use, the goal is the same: the shopper should never have to guess.


**7. Ask for size at the right point in the personalization flow**


Place the size option **before or alongside** the personalization options, not after. Shoppers make the sizing decision while they're still paying attention, instead of rushing it as a final step.


There's a second reason, and it's the one most stores miss: on many products, the design itself depends on the size. A name centered on an adult Large can end up too close to the seams on a toddler 2T. A photo cropped for an 8x10 canvas won't fit a 16x20 canvas, because the proportions are different. If the shopper personalizes first and picks a size later, the design they approved may not be the design that gets printed. We'll cover how to fix this below.


**8. Confirm size before checkout**


Give shoppers one last chance to catch a mistake:


- Add a short note near the Add to cart button: "Personalized items are made to order. Please double-check your size."
- Make sure the cart shows the selected size next to the personalization details.
- Repeat the size clearly in the order confirmation email, so a wrong choice can be fixed before production starts.


## Match the design to the size, not just the size chart


A size chart helps shoppers choose the right size. But on personalized products, that's only half the job. The design also has to fit the size they chose, both in the preview and in the final print.


This is where your product personalizer matters. With[Customily](https://www.customily.com/) , you can change the design area or the whole template based on the size the shopper selects:


- **A template for each size.** Set up a different template or print area for each size option. When a shopper switches from S to XL, or from 8x10 to 16x20, the live preview switches to that size's layout right away.
- **A preview that matches what ships.** Shoppers see their name, photo or artwork on the exact size they're buying. That means fewer "it looked different on the website" complaints, and fewer remakes.
- **Print files at the right size.** Customily generates a print-ready file for every order, based on the size that was ordered. Your production team doesn't have to resize designs by hand, which is where many sizing mistakes happen after the order is placed.
- **The same personalization options on every size.** Your Image uploader (for customer photos) and Dynamic images (artwork, clipart and icon options) can be set up on each size's template, so shoppers get the same experience whatever size they pick.


#### Where size-based templates make the biggest difference


- [Kids' and adult apparel](https://www.customily.com/sell-personalized-products/t-shirts) **in one listing.** Smaller sizes need a smaller print area, so names and numbers stay centered and readable.
- [Canvas prints, posters and frames](https://www.customily.com/sell-personalized-products/wall-art-canvas) **.** Different sizes often have different proportions. A template for each size makes sure the customer's photo is cropped correctly before they buy.
- [Blankets and pillows](https://www.customily.com/sell-personalized-products/home-decor) **.** A throw and a king-size blanket need very different layouts for the same photo collage.
- **Pet tags and accessories.** Small and large tags leave very different space for a name and phone number, so the shopper sees right away if their text fits.


The result: the size chart helps the shopper pick the right size, and the size-based template makes sure the design is right for that size. Together, they cover both ways a custom order can go wrong.

#### Sizing tips by product type


Sizing looks different depending on what you sell. A few quick notes:


Product type What shoppers need to know


Adult apparel Chest, length and sleeve measurements; fit notes (unisex, slim, relaxed)


Kids' apparel Age ranges plus measurements; a note on whether to size up for growth


Rings and jewelry A ring size guide, chain length options, and how to measure at home


Pet products Neck or chest measurement, with a clear "how to measure your pet" tip


Home and decor Exact dimensions of blankets, frames, canvases and pillows, ideally with a scale reference


For home and decor, sizing isn't about fit, but it causes just as many complaints. A "large" canvas means very different things to different shoppers, so always show dimensions.


#### Gift buyers need extra help


A big share of personalized orders are gifts, and gift buyers often don't know the recipient's size. A few ways to help them:


- Suggest sizing up on items like hoodies and sweatshirts, where a slightly loose fit is usually fine.
- Use age ranges for kids' items instead of numeric sizes alone.
- For rings, explain how to borrow a ring the recipient already wears and measure it.
- Promote one-size-fits-all products (mugs, blankets, ornaments, tote bags) as safe gift options.


#### Use your order data to improve your charts


Your size charts shouldn't be set once and forgotten. Track why customers contact you about sizing or ask for remakes. If one product keeps getting "too small" complaints, add a fit note, update the measurements, or recommend sizing up. A few small fixes on your best-selling products can noticeably reduce remakes.


#### Quick checklist


- ✅ Size chart link sits right next to the size selector
- ✅ Each product (or blank) has its own chart
- ✅ Real measurements are shown, with a how-to-measure tip
- ✅ Centimeters and inches are both available
- ✅ Fit notes are visible near the size options
- ✅ A size recommendation is available for unsure shoppers
- ✅ Size comes before or alongside personalization
- ✅ Size is confirmed in the cart and the confirmation email


## Get the size right before you personalize


Personalized products are made for one person, so getting the size right matters more than with anything else you sell. Clear charts, product-specific measurements, plain-language fit notes and a smart order of options will prevent most sizing mistakes before they happen.

### Frequently Asked Questions: Sizing on personalized products


**Where should I put the size chart on a product page?**


Right next to the size selector. A "Size chart" button or link beside the size options gets far more use than a link in the footer or a separate page. If shoppers have to leave the product page to check measurements, many will guess instead.


**Do I need a different size chart for each product?**


Yes, if your products use different blanks or suppliers. A T-shirt and a hoodie from two different suppliers won't fit the same, even if both are labeled Medium. For print-on-demand products, use the measurements from the supplier's spec sheet for that exact blank.


**Should I accept returns on personalized products?**


Most stores don't, because a personalized item can't be resold. Whatever your policy is, show it clearly near the size selector and the Add to cart button. A clear policy plus good sizing information builds more trust than a vague policy hidden in the footer.


**What should I do when a customer orders the wrong size on a personalized item?**


First, check whether the mistake came from your size chart or fit notes. If the chart was wrong or unclear, a free remake is usually the right call, and you should fix the chart right away. If the customer simply picked the wrong size, many stores offer a remake at a discount. Either way, track the reason so you can spot products that keep causing problems.


**Can the design change based on the size the customer picks?**


Yes. With Customily, you can set a different template or design area for each size. When the shopper changes the size, the live preview switches to that size's layout, so they see exactly how their name, photo or artwork will look on the size they're buying.


**How do I make sure the print file matches the size that was ordered?**


Use a personalizer that generates print files based on the selected size. Customily creates a print-ready file for every order using the template for the size that was ordered, so your team doesn't have to resize designs by hand.
